newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-YORK ADD EVERTON TO LIST OF VICTIMS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-YORK ADD EVERTON TO LIST OF VICTIMS.

text.p: York City were cast in the familiar role of English League Cup giantkillers on Tuesday as premier league side Everton suffered an embarrassingly similar fate to Manchester United last year.

The second division club, who achieved a famous 3-0 victory at Old Trafford last season which paved the way to a 4-3 aggregate win over United, repeated the trick against Everton by the same scoreline after clinching the second leg 3-2.

Everton, held to a 1-1 draw in the first leg a week ago, went a goal ahead after 24 minutes through Paul Rideout but then allowed York's Neil Tolson, Gary Bull and Graeme Murty to put the tie out of their reach.

A last-minute goal from Gary Speed narrowed York's winning margin but could not prevent them extending an impressive list which also included Arsenal in the F.A. Cup in 1985. Ironically, the Yorkshire side had to wait until the final match of last season to escape relegation.
It was another dire night for Manchester City, beaten 1-0 at home and 5-1 on aggregate by third division Lincoln City whose goal came from Dutchman Gijsbert Bos, and the entire city of Sheffield.

Both Wednesday and United suffered bad defeats, Wednesday slipping up 1-0 to former striker Nigel Jemson's 85th-minute goal at Oxford and United crashing 5-2 at home against Stockport County, already 2-1 up from the first leg.

Middlesbrough were able to stroll into the third round, winning 3-0 at Hereford to secure a 10-0 aggregate success, Danish striker Mikkel Beck scoring on his debut and Brazilian Branco adding the third direct from a corner.
